newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC SEES HIGHER BASE METALS OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC SEES HIGHER BASE METALS OUTPUT.

text.p: Gold and base metals miner WMC Ld said on Wednesday it saw higher base metals production but lower gold production and lower costs for business as a whole in the 1997/98 (July/June) year.

"In terms of volume, there should be more metal produced. The major change this year is we don't expect to have any interruptions for nickel production which should be running at its expanded capacity," Morgan told reporters.
Morgan said gold production would be lower due to the sale of the high cost Hill 50 mine in Australia.
He said although alumina prices were currently not much different than the previous financal year the company saw an upward trend emerging.
"The net effect at present is the average price for alumina is a few dollars higher than in the previous corresponding period. There is no doubt that the trend is up." Morgan said.
In respect of costs, Morgan said WMC expected a much better result due to lower costs from its gold operations and from its alumina business.
Morgan said the biggest change in terms of outlook for production would be in 1999 when the company's Olympic Dam copper/uranium expansion came on line in Western Australia.
Morgan would not comment on the overall outlook for the company, saying the variability of metal prices made it impossible to predict earnings so far ahead.
WMC earlier reported a 23 percent fall in full year equity net profit of A$297.2 million, struck on 7.5 percent lower sales of A$2.17 billion.
By 2.05 p.m. (0405 GMT), WMC shares were one cent higher at A$7.43 on turnover of 2.9 million shares.
